title: Finite mass measure of a finite-mass current, agreeing with local mass on open balls
statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and let T ∈ D_n(ℝ^P) (T : GeometricCurrentOn univ n on ℝ^P = Eucl P) have finite mass M(T) = T.mass < ∞. Then there is a measure μ on ℝ^P with μ(ℝ^P) ≤ M(T) and μ(B_r(x)) = M_{B_r(x)}(T) (= T.massOn (ball x r)) for every x ∈ ℝ^P and every r ∈ ℝ, where B_r(x) is the open ball (empty when r ≤ 0).
lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (T : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Eucl P)) n), T.mass < ∞ → ∃ μ : Measure (Eucl P), μ univ ≤ T.mass ∧ ∀ (x : Eucl P) (r : ℝ), μ (ball x r) = T.massOn (ball x r)
